newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - US CPI, housing starts get look Oct 11 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US CPI, housing starts get look Oct 11 wk.

text.p: Friday's U.S. producer price report stole some thunder from next week's consumer price data but may have elevated the status of Thursday's housing starts release, said economists in a Reuters poll.

On average, 24 experts forecast overall CPI rose 0.3 percent in September after a 0.1-percent August rise. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, also rose 0.3 percent, they forecast.

The higher September consumer prices might not cause too much of a stir, since investors already adjusted in response to the September Producer Price Index (PPI), said Joe Lavorgna, an economist at Lehman Government Securities Inc.
Core PPI rose 0.3 percent last month after a 0.1 percent decline in August.
"Because you had (producer price) data that weren't all that friendly, it's possible you got some of that inflation trade (on Friday)," Lavorgna said.
Besides, economists said, the projected jump in CPI can be attributed to special factors and should be temporary.

"There are two factors: a reversal of the 1.4-percent drop in apparel (prices in August), and the 10.0 percent airline tax kicking in," said John Park, an economist at Sanwa Securities (USA) Co. "The next few numbers should be moderate."
With CPI growth already in the cards, other data will get a closer look. "The markets will concentrate more on housing numbers," said Lavorgna.
The experts projected housing starts fell to an annual rate of 1.47 million units last month from 1.525 million in August.
